key_insight: 3D opto-electro-thermal simulation shows that lead-free MgXS3 chalcogenide perovskites can deliver high-efficiency solar cells, with device performance strongly controlled by thickness, doping, defects, and an Sb2S3 BSF layer.
engineering_relevance: The study provides practical design rules for optimizing realistic, thermally coupled perovskite solar-cell architectures without relying on toxic lead-based absorbers.
method: 3D finite-element COMSOL simulation of a ZnSe/MgXS3/Sb2S3 stack
Self-consistent coupling of optical generation, drift-diffusion transport, and heat transfer under AM 1.5G 1-sun illumination
Systematic sweeps of absorber thickness, doping, defect density, and BSF effects
evidence_signal: Optimized devices reached simulated PCEs of 28.18% (MgZrS3), 26.72% (MgTiS3), and 28.16% (MgHfS3), with corresponding VOC, JSC, and FF reported in the abstract.
watch_item: Results are simulation-based and depend on model assumptions, so experimental validation and material quality control will be critical before practical deployment.
paper_title: Numerical exploration on unveiling the photovoltaic potential of MgXS3(X = Ti, Zr, Hf) chalcogenide perovskites
